capex_pct_revenue.caveat: Full-year 2026 revenue not yet disclosed (2026 in progress); capex guidance is a FY figure compared here against a single quarter's revenue, not annual revenue. Not a true annual capex/revenue ratio.
capex_pct_revenue.revenue_source: Meta Q2 2026 earnings call / report, Aug 3 2026 (via CNBC, GuruFocus coverage)
capex_pct_revenue.capex_guidance_source: Meta Q1 2026 earnings call (capex guidance raised, Apr 2026); ceiling confirmed Meta Q2 2026 report, Aug 3 2026 (CNBC)

strategy_timeline.event: MTIA (Meta Training and Inference Accelerator) first introduced as Meta's homegrown AI chip family
strategy_timeline.what_it_means: Meta begins building an alternative to buying 100% of its AI compute from Nvidia/AMD, starting with internal ranking/recommendation workloads.

strategy_timeline.event_date_display: ~2 weeks before Mar 11 2026 (exact date not disclosed)
strategy_timeline.event: Meta signs a long-term AI infrastructure agreement with AMD for additional GPU capacity
strategy_timeline.what_it_means: Roughly two weeks before announcing its custom-silicon acceleration, Meta locks in more third-party GPU supply — evidence this is additive ('portfolio approach'), not a pivot away from GPUs.
strategy_timeline.source: Meta long-term AI infrastructure agreement with AMD, ~late Feb 2026 (reported ahead of Mar 11 2026 MTIA announcement) — exact date not disclosed; timing stated only as '~2 weeks before' the Mar 11 2026 MTIA announcement

strategy_timeline.event: Meta announces acceleration to four MTIA chip generations (300/400/450/500) in two years
strategy_timeline.what_it_means: A much faster public cadence than typical multi-year chip cycles; Meta's own stated rationale is supply diversity and price insulation versus sole reliance on Nvidia/AMD, optimized for high-volume, predictable inference TCO — not a claim that this reduces total capex.
strategy_timeline.source: Meta Engineering blog, about.fb.com, Mar 11 2026; CNBC, Mar 11 2026 (Meta VP of Engineering, on the record)

strategy_timeline.event: 2026 full-year capex guidance raised to $125B-$145B; Meta cuts 8,000 jobs (~10% of workforce) and removes 6,000 open roles
strategy_timeline.what_it_means: Meta is simultaneously increasing AI infrastructure spend and cutting headcount elsewhere in the business, explicitly to 'offset the other investments we're making' — the labor cuts are a direct funding offset for the capex ramp, not a sign of broader retrenchment.
strategy_timeline.source: Meta Q1 2026 earnings call (capex guidance raised, Apr 2026); ceiling confirmed Meta Q2 2026 report, Aug 3 2026 (CNBC); Meta workforce reduction announcement, Apr 2026 (CNBC)

strategy_timeline.event: Meta expands its silicon partnership with Broadcom to co-develop future MTIA generations (multi-generation agreement)
strategy_timeline.what_it_means: Meta locks in a chip-design partner for multiple future MTIA generations, signaling this is a durable multi-year program rather than a one-off chip project.

strategy_timeline.event: Q2 2026 results: revenue +28% YoY to $60.8B, but free cash flow down ~91% YoY and net income down 14% YoY; $145B capex ceiling confirmed
strategy_timeline.what_it_means: The capex-vs-cash-flow tension that motivated the April efficiency push has not eased by the next quarter's report — the pressure the silicon strategy is meant to address is still visibly present in the same period MTIA is scaling up.
strategy_timeline.source: Meta Q2 2026 earnings call / report, Aug 3 2026 (via CNBC, GuruFocus coverage)

addressable_share.framing_type: Order-of-magnitude framing, not a precise estimate
addressable_share.cited_industry_estimate: Inference ~ two-thirds of AI compute in 2026
addressable_share.estimate_source: Deloitte estimate, cited by TechBrew, Mar 2026
addressable_share.mtia_scope: MTIA 400/450/500 target inference (GenAI) workloads only; frontier LLM training remains GPU-bound
addressable_share.conclusion: At most ~2/3 of AI compute is theoretically addressable by custom silicon today; the remaining ~1/3 (frontier-LLM training) is out of MTIA's disclosed scope regardless of chip performance
addressable_share.disclosure_gap: Meta has not disclosed its own training/inference compute split or a capex dollar split by silicon type -- this framing cannot be converted into a dollar figure
